transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time for this consultation. As you know, the Mosaic ERG and the Bridge ERG have proposed combining their monthly programming under a shared charter. Before I make a decision, I want to hear from each of you — the ERG representatives, Employee Relations, Accessibility, and People Policy — so we can work through any concerns or conditions together. Let's start with the ERG representatives: can you walk us through what motivated this proposal and what the combined structure would look like?

transcript.text: Thanks, Marisol. I'd prefer to share the specifics once we've heard from the ERG representatives, so we have the full context of what's being proposed. I don't want to get ahead of that conversation, but I did want to signal early that ER may have a condition or recommendation to discuss.

transcript.text: Thanks, Marisol, and thanks everyone for the thoughtful flags already. Let me walk you through the proposal from the ERG side. The motivation here is practical: Mosaic and Bridge have seen significant overlap in membership and programming themes over the past year. We've been coordinating informally on several events, and the idea emerged that rather than duplicating efforts, we could combine our monthly programming under one shared charter — pooling resources, reducing scheduling conflicts for shared members, and creating a more cohesive community experience. Under the proposed structure, we'd maintain a single monthly meeting instead of two separate ones, with co-facilitated leadership drawing from both existing leadership groups. The shared charter would outline programming goals, governance, and decision-making processes. We'd consolidate the mailing lists so communications go through one channel. That said, I want to be transparent that there's an important commitment I made to Mosaic members that I need to put on the table formally now. I promised them — in a group meeting, though it wasn't added to the written proposal — that I would only support a merger if members received a written charter and the arrangement had a formal review after exactly 90 days. I want to make sure that commitment is part of this consultation.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From my accessibility observations, I've noted that several prospective participants need recordings and asynchronous access to meetings, and I personally cannot reliably attend meetings beginning after 3:00 p.m. These access needs have not been raised in the merger proposal because the groups usually schedule their own meetings, but they're directly relevant to how a combined monthly meeting would be structured.

transcript.text: Thanks, Talia. From a People Policy perspective, I want to note how the two-thirds opt-in vote requirement interacts with what you've just described. Since the merger would consolidate mailing lists and combine leadership groups, both existing memberships would need to understand what they're voting on — which means the written charter you committed to providing would likely need to be available to members before the opt-in votes take place. That way, voting members in each ERG can make an informed decision about whether to join the combined structure. I'd also flag that the 90-day formal review you mentioned aligns well with standard policy practice for new governance arrangements, but I'd want to make sure the review process is documented in the charter itself so members know what to expect when they cast their votes. I don't have additional conditions beyond the opt-in vote requirement I've already shared, but I do think the sequencing — charter finalized, then separate votes in each group, then launch — is something we should be explicit about.

transcript.text: Thanks, Marisol. I appreciate the opportunity to share this now, and I want to be thoughtful about how I frame it given the confidentiality involved. During a confidential Employee Relations intake this month, a Mosaic member described an unresolved interpersonal conflict with a Bridge co-chair. Specifically, the member stated they would not attend meetings chaired by that individual. This intake has not yet been shared with you, Marisol, because the member asked that it first be handled through a structured process. I'm surfacing the existence of this concern now because it's directly relevant to the proposed combined structure — particularly the co-facilitated leadership model and the single monthly meeting. If one of the co-facilitators is the Bridge co-chair in question, this member — and potentially others with similar concerns — may effectively be excluded from participation. I want to be clear that I'm not sharing the identities involved or the specific details of the conflict out of respect for the member's confidentiality request. However, I do think this has implications for the conditions of approval. My recommendation would be that, as part of the combined structure, there be a clear process for rotating or sharing facilitation duties in a way that ensures no member feels unable to attend based on who is chairing a given meeting. I'd also recommend that the 90-day review Talia mentioned specifically include a check on whether any participation barriers have emerged. I'm not in a position to disclose more detail in this setting, but I'm available to discuss the intake privately, Marisol, if you'd like to explore whether additional conditions are warranted before you finalize your decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Evan. I appreciate you surfacing that concern, and I want to respond from the ERG side. First, on the commitment I made to Mosaic members — I want to formally restate that the written charter and the 90-day formal review are non-negotiable for me in terms of supporting this merger. I promised that to Mosaic members in a group meeting, and I need to honor it. I'm glad to see it aligns with what Grant and others have raised about sequencing and informed voting. Second, regarding Evan's recommendation about facilitation rotation — I think that's a reasonable and important safeguard to build into the charter. If there's a risk that any member feels unable to attend based on who is chairing, that undermines the whole purpose of combining these groups. I'd support including a rotating facilitation model and a participation barrier check as part of the 90-day review. Marisol, I'd also want to make sure that before the opt-in votes Grant described, the charter clearly lays out all of these conditions — the 90-day review, the facilitation approach, the accessibility accommodations Noor raised, and the review criteria — so members are voting with full transparency. I don't think I have additional conditions beyond what's already been discussed, but I want to make sure the charter I promised members is comprehensive enough to address everything raised in this consultation.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Talia. I appreciate your commitment to making the charter comprehensive. From the Accessibility standpoint, I want to make sure the specific access needs I raised are explicitly written into the charter rather than left to be determined after launch. That means the charter should commit to: providing recordings of all meetings, ensuring asynchronous participation options for anyone who cannot attend live, and scheduling the combined monthly meeting so it begins no later than 3:00 p.m. These shouldn't be framed as optional accommodations to be worked out later — they should be baseline design principles for the combined structure from day one. I'd also echo Talia's point that these need to be visible in the charter before the opt-in votes, so members who have similar access needs — whether they've raised them or not — can see that the combined structure will work for them before they vote. I don't have additional conditions beyond what I've already shared, but I do want to flag that access needs like these often go unspoken, so the charter's commitment to them matters both practically and as a signal of inclusion.
